headline: All majors below the 200-day line with mixed momentum; whales moving coins onto exchanges while funding remains expensive and skewed long.
paragraphs: The regime is underwater across the board. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, Doge, and Cardano are all trading below their 200-day simple moving averages, and none of them has crossed above it. There is no golden cross anywhere in the set. This is a downtrend regime, full stop. Bitcoin sits 49.7 percent below its 12-month high of $124,740, Ethereum 61.1 percent below $4,818. The weaker names are worse: Cardano trades 81.5 percent off its high at $0.1786, Doge 75.9 percent off. The total market cap is down 0.73 percent on the day to $2.245 trillion, and Bitcoin dominance holds firm at 56.1 percent, meaning the losses are broad, not concentrated in alts.

Momentum is split and mostly tired. Bitcoin's RSI-14 sits at 41.7, below the 50 midpoint and well clear of oversold, which means sellers have room to push but buyers are not panicked yet. The MACD is below signal, confirming downward pressure. Ethereum's RSI is at the midpoint, 49.6, with MACD also below signal, a picture of stalled motion. The real split lives in the smaller caps: Solana and BNB both show MACD above signal (a bullish cross), but Solana is also underwater on the 200-day and underwater in price action. Doge, too, has MACD above signal but is down 6.07 percent over 30 days and 75.9 percent from its high. These crosses between momentum and trend are not confirmations of reversal; they are early whispers of a potential bounce off low levels, but nothing has broken the downtrend yet.

Derivatives positioning is expensive and crowded to the long side. Bitcoin funding stands at 8.9 percent annualized, and Ethereum at 8.6 percent; these are rates above the historical median, meaning longs are paying a premium to hold their bets. The long-short ratio on Bitcoin is 2.25 to 1, on Ethereum 1.95 to 1, on XRP a stretched 3.54 to 1, and on Doge an extreme 5.46 to 1. Open interest is substantial: Bitcoin has $2.15 billion on OKX alone, Ethereum $1.36 billion. The liquidation picture over the last 21-24 hours shows heavy bias: Bitcoin has flushed $6.04 million in long liquidations versus $1.59 million in short, a 3.8-to-1 ratio; Ethereum shows $3.12 million in longs versus $1.21 million in shorts, a 2.6-to-1 ratio. When price drops on funded longs with crowded positioning, the liquidation waterfall follows. Solana is the exception: funding is negative at minus 3.8 percent annualized, meaning shorts are paying; it has liquidated $1.18 million in longs against only $17,544 in shorts, a sign the long crowding is specific to the coin, not a symptom of market-wide risk appetite.

Whale flows and stablecoin reserves paint a tension worth naming. Over the last 72 hours, whales have moved $262.8 million net onto exchanges, primarily Bitcoin: $127.5 million to Coinbase institutional and $117.4 million to Binance. This is selling pressure, not accumulation from cold. Stablecoins on exchanges total $306.3 billion, down only 0.69 percent over 30 days, so dry powder has not evaporated, but it is also not stacking. The six-week whale flow rolling window shows volatility: plus $244.8 million, plus $1.06 billion, plus $315.7 million, then minus $342.2 million one week ago. The net-onto-exchanges move this week counters the recent pattern, suggesting a shift in whale posture from accumulation back to distribution. Institutional flows on the ETF side confirm unease: Bitcoin spot ETFs saw a net outflow of $131.1 million on August 13 and $227.3 million over the last five sessions, with only two consecutive days of outflows, so the pattern is not persistent yet. Ethereum ETFs, by contrast, took in $5.9 million on August 13 and $46.6 million over five sessions, suggesting some rotation into the second-largest asset.

Sentiment sits in Fear at 29, the 30-day range 25 to 33, so the crowd is scared but not panicked. The disconnect here is worth noting: fear gauge says anxiety; the tape shows whales loading coins onto exchanges and Bitcoin fundingremaining elevated while longs dominate the leverage stack. This is a classic misalignment: crowd emotion lags the money move. When the crowd finally catches the whale direction, or when whales sense the crowd catching on, the next impulse clarifies.

Watch for three things. First, a reclaim of the 200-day line on Bitcoin or Ethereum would signal a regime break upward; neither is close. Second, funding rates, especially on Bitcoin and Ethereum: if they roll from positive to negative, longs are no longer paying a premium and the crowding begins to unwind structurally. Third, the direction of whale flows over the next one to two days: another move onto exchanges confirms the distribution thesis; a reversal back into cold storage signals a floor and accumulation. The network is functioning smoothly (fees down to $4-$5, difficulty adjusting down 3.2 percent), so no operational friction is adding to the pressure.
